content.user_title: Manage Google Tasks from AI Workflows
content.value_statement: Teams need fast access to Google Tasks without leaving their AI assistant. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code inspect commands and manage lists or tasks through gws.
actual_capabilities: Lists Google Tasks task lists for the authenticated user.
Creates, gets, updates, patches, and deletes task lists.
Lists, creates, gets, updates, patches, moves, and deletes tasks.
Clears completed tasks from a selected task list.
Guides users to inspect method schemas before building parameters.
Uses gws tasks and gws schema command patterns.
limitations: Requires the gws CLI and valid Google Workspace authentication.
Does not create assigned tasks from Docs or Chat Spaces through the Tasks API.
Cannot bypass Google Tasks quota and item limits.
Needs schema inspection before complex parameters are submitted.

use_cases.title: Organize Personal Task Lists
use_cases.description: Create a new task list, add tasks, and move items into a useful order.

use_cases.title: Maintain Team Follow-Ups
use_cases.description: Review open tasks, update due details, and clear completed work after a project checkpoint.

use_cases.title: Audit Task API Parameters
use_cases.description: Inspect gws method schemas before sending task updates with required parameters.

prompt_templates.title: List My Task Lists
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my Google Tasks task lists and summarize the names I can choose from.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a task titled [task title] in my [task list name] list, then confirm where it was added.

prompt_templates.title: Update and Move Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the task [task title], update its details to [new details], and move it under [parent task] if supported.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Schema First
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the schema for tasks.[resource].[method], identify required parameters, and propose the safest command before running it.

output_examples.output: The assistant returns available task lists, including titles and identifiers when available, then asks which list to inspect next.

output_examples.input: Add a task to follow up with finance tomorrow.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks the task creation schema, creates the requested task in the selected list, and confirms the result.

output_examples.input: Clear completed tasks from my project list.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the target list, runs the clear operation, and reports that completed tasks are now hidden from default listing.

best_practices: Inspect the gws schema for each method before using new parameters.
Confirm destructive actions such as delete or clear before running them.
Use exact task list names or identifiers to avoid changing the wrong list.
anti_patterns: Do not run delete or clear operations without explicit user confirmation.
Do not assume assigned tasks can be created through the Tasks Public API.
Do not submit complex parameters before checking the method schema.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages Google Tasks task lists and individual tasks through the gws CLI.

faq.question: Does it require Google authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The gws CLI must be installed and authenticated for the target Google Workspace account.

faq.question: Can it delete tasks or lists?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents delete operations, so users should confirm destructive actions before execution.

faq.question: Can it work with assigned tasks from Docs or Chat?
faq.answer: It can list some assigned tasks, but the Tasks Public API cannot create assigned tasks from those surfaces.

faq.question: How should I build command parameters?
faq.answer: Use gws schema for the target resource and method before choosing params or JSON flags.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
